question.worked_solution:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $\sqrt{2c-1}-2.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $\sqrt{2c-1}-2,$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4{c}^{2}-25}{\sqrt{2c-1}+2} & = \\ \frac{4{c}^{2}-25}{\sqrt{2c-1}+2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2c-1}-2}{\sqrt{2c-1}-2} & = \\ \frac{(4{c}^{2}-25)(\sqrt{2c-1}-2)}{(\sqrt{2c-1}+2)(\sqrt{2c-1}-2)} & = \\ \frac{(4{c}^{2}-25)(\sqrt{2c-1}-2)}{(\sqrt{2c-1})^{2}-{2}^{2}} & = \\ \frac{(2c+5)(2c-5)(\sqrt{2c-1}-2)}{2c-1-4} & = \\ \frac{(2c+5)(2c-5)(\sqrt{2c-1}-2)}{2c-5} & = \\ \frac{(2c+5)\cancel{(2c-5)}(\sqrt{2c-1}-2)}{\cancel{2c-5}} & = \\ (2c+5)(\sqrt{2c-1}-2)\end{aligned}
$$
